title: Biography
description:
The Du Ponts: America's Wealthiest Family
Portrait of the fabulously wealthy family that built an empire in chemicals. Looks at why most family members have shunned publicity.

title: Biography
description:
Neiman Marcus: Last of the Merchant Kings
Story of a brother and sister--Carrie Neiman and Herbert Marcus--who overcame great odds to establish one of the greatest quality merchandise stores in the world.

title: Biography
description:
Faberge: Imperial Jeweler
Story of Russia's Peter Carl Faberge, who created the fabled jeweled eggs that are worth millions today. Traces his life from the time he worked for the czars to his escape to Switzerland after the Russian Revolution.

title: Biography
description:
Andrew Carnegie: Prince of Steel
The life and career of the great 19th-century industrialist and philanthropist. The son of a poor Scottish immigrant, Carnegie built an empire in steel manufacturing before being bought out by US Steel.

title: Biography
description:
J. Pierpont Morgan
Story of the 19th-century power broker who once controlled 70 percent of all the steel and 60 percent of all stocks in America.

title: Biography
description:
J.W. Marriott
Born into a family of faith and poverty, early in life J. Willard Marriott shouldered a man's responsibilities. Learn the story of the lanky Utahan who inched his way into corporate America as his 9-stool rootbeer stand grew into a billion-dollar hotel and restaurant chain. His sons and friend Reverend Billy Graham offer insight.

title: Biography
description:
R.H. Macy
Saga of the Nantucket merchant who overcame early failures to help create the modern department store and launch the national retail chain that bears his name.

title: Biography
description:
Calvin Klein: A Stylish Obsession
Calvin Klein was born on November 19, 1942, in Bronx, New York. He studied fashion in New York City and apprenticed for a suit manufacturer. In 1968, he opened his own company. He was initially recognized for suits and coats, but his sportswear line became popular as well.

title: Grant
description:
Unlikely Hero
In one of the unlikeliest stories in American history, Ulysses S. Grant rises from his humble beginnings to become the winning General in one of the Civil War's bloodiest battles.

title: Grant
description:
Lincoln's General
With his back up against the wall, Ulysses S. Grant takes incredible risks, becomes Abraham Lincoln's favorite General, and prepares for an epic clash with Robert E. Lee.

title: Grant
description:
Freedom's Champion
Ulysses S. Grant defeats Robert E. Lee and wins the Civil War, only to find that he will be called to duty again to serve as President during one of the most difficult times in America history.

title: Story Feature
description:
Lee & Grant
Produced with the cooperation of leading Civil War historian Winston Groom, author of Forrest Gump, this 2-hour special is a personal look at two iconic leaders of the Civil War.

title: American Restoration
description:
Buck Wild
Rick and Ron take restoration by the horns when they agree to revive a vintage mechanical bull. Can they stay steadily astride this rough ride, or will they be bucked off?

title: American Restoration
description:
The Big Move
When a client hefts in a 1900s penny scale from the Santa Cruz boardwalk, Rick and his crew tighten their belts. Can they successfully slim down this massive mechanism, or will their weighty workload tip the scales?

title: American Restoration
description:
Bumper Balls
After Rick agrees to restore a vintage Italian bumper car from a local antique shop, the shop braces for immediate impact. Can they effectively electrify this dented delight, or will this entertaining endeavor give them whiplash?

title: American Restoration
description:
Cold Cuts
Rick and his crew sharpen their service skills when a client ships in a 1900s Berkel meat slicer. Can they carefully carve out a mechanical masterpiece, or will they lose a few fingers on this slice-and-dice device?

title: American Restoration
description:
The Big Bang
Rick and the guys aim to please when an 1800s cannon rolls into the shop. Can they hit their transformation target, or will this banged up blaster backfire?

title: American Restoration
description:
Top Dog
Rick prepares for battle when a 1940s dog tag maker comes into the shop.

title: American Restoration
description:
Pump and Gun
Rick and his crew take a shot in the dark when a 1943 trap machine lands in the shop.

title: American Restoration
description:
Tall Order
Rick faces a larger-than-life restoration when a client lugs in a 1930s Pep Boys marquee to the shop. Can he tackle this towering task, or will these famous figures turn into a colossal catastrophe?

title: American Restoration
description:
Blast Off
Rick takes on the biggest challenge of his career when a 1960s rocket slide comes into the shop piece by giant piece.

title: American Restoration
description:
Tyler's Promotion
Rick and his crew face a sticky situation when a cement gun from 1915 rolls into the shop. Can they safely seal up this concrete-hurtling contraption?

title: American Restoration
description:
King of Signs
While Rick is away from the shop, his brother Ron takes matters into his own hands when a client brings in a 1900s love tester. Is this a match made in overhaul heaven, or will this romantic restoration break his heart?

title: American Restoration
description:
Hot and Salty
The heat is on for Rick and his crew when they restore a salty 1960s popcorn machine. Can they freshen up this corny contraption?

title: American Restoration
description:
Treats and Feet
Rick battles a brain freeze when a 1940s Good Humor bicycle pedals into the shop. Can he deliver a sweet solution to this sticky situation?

title: American Restoration
description:
Restoration Rivalry
Rick and his son Tyler kick off a restoration race after a pair of vintage scooters wheels into the shop. Can Tyler show up his dear ol' dad, or will Rick prove father always knows best?

title: American Restoration
description:
Cannonball Safe
Rick and his guys get keyed up to restore a colossal 1920s cannonball safe. Can they lock up this protected project, or will this massive mission be too heavy to handle?

title: The Master
description:
Konrad Seusenhofer: Master Armorer
The toughest and lightest suits of armor, as well as the most beautiful, were those created by German-born Konrad Seusenhofer at the beginning of the 16th century for his patron, the Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian I.

title: The Master
description:
James of St. George: Master of Castles
The castles built by French-born master builder James of St. George in the 13th century have survived intact for more than seven centuries.

title: The Master
description:
Joseph Manton: Master Gunsmith
Most gun enthusiasts agree that the finest sporting guns of all time were those made by English gunsmith Joseph Manton in the late 18th and early 19th century. From his London workshop, he produced guns for rich and royal clients.

title: The Master
description:
Don Emilio Solanet: The Horse Master
The horse synonymous with the Argentine Gaucho is the Criollo, descended from horses brought from Spain to the American continent by the conquistadors.

title: Ancient Mysteries
description:
Camelot
Were King Arthur and his Knights of the Round Table fictional characters or real people? This fascinating hour takes viewers on a magical quest through England and Wales in search of clues that Arthur, Queen Guinevere, Sir Lancelot, and Merlin the Magician actually existed.

title: History's Mysteries
description:
The Knights of Camelot
King Arthur, Merlin, Lancelot, Guinevere, and the Knights of the Round Table--are they figures from fanciful fable or portraits from a pagan past? Travel back to early England and Wales to unravel the Arthurian legend and learn why the yearning for Camelot and chivalry survives.

title: Story Feature
description:
Knights and Armor
Fascinating documentary that tells the colorful story of medieval knights. Location filming, reconstructions, and original music recall the battles, the armor, the tournaments, the chivalry, and the romance that made the knight one of history's most intriguing characters.

title: America's Secret Slang
description:
Straight From the Horse's Mouth
In this episode, we look at the ways that American English has been transformed by animals, food, sports--and death. Ever wonder why we say "that's a horse of a different color" or "that's for the birds"? Why do we "chew the fat" when we talk or "put up our dukes" when we fight? And why, when we die, do we "kick the bucket"? All these terms show the ways that American English has evolved and mutated through the animals we raise, the food we eat, the games we play, and the end we want to avoid. Zach Selwyn hosts.

title: America's Secret Slang
description:
Lower the Boom
In this episode, we look at the ways that American English was transformed by the high seas, the ancient world, the movers and shakers of big business, and the news industry. Ever wonder why we're "pooped" when we're tired? Or say that a drunk is "three sheets to the wind"? Why do we say our "ears are burning" if someone's talking about us, and why is October the 10th month, even though its name means "8th"? Why is a rich, powerful person called a "tycoon"? And why are those supermarket scandal sheets called "tabloids"? All these terms show the powerful impact that sailing, big business, the ancient world, and the news media have had on American English.

title: America's Secret Slang
description:
Riding Shotgun
Every day we use words and phrases that come from deep within our history. Their origins reveal a lot about us and where we came from, but most of us have no idea what these terms originally meant. In this episode we look at how forms of transportation from horses to trains to cars, and different intoxicating substances from opium to booze, influenced the common words and phrases we say every day. Why do insensitive people "ride roughshod" over others, while lucky people ride the "gravy train?" Who put the jay in "jaywalker," and the bus in "busboy"? Why are "highways" high, what do "turnpikes" turn, and why is a wild person "hell on wheels"?  When it comes to substances, who put the hero in heroin, the junk in junkie, and the ooze in booze? And what's the connection between George Washington and the words grog and groggy?

title: America's Secret Slang
description:
Cut to the Chase
In this episode we look at how entertainment from circuses and vaudeville to plays and movies influenced the common words and phrases we say every day. How did bad actors give us the word "explode," rude actors give us the phrase "to upstage" someone, and superstitious actors give us "break a leg?" How did the circus give us words like "jumbo" and "Siamese twins," and the idea that politicians "jump on the bandwagon?" Why did vaudeville invent "deadpan" humor, "slapstick" comedy, and "off color jokes?" And how did the movies give us expressions like "cut to the chase" and "cliffhanger"?
